title: Computing and Plotting the Logistic Sigmoid Curve
description: Evaluate the logistic sigmoid across the supplied evenly spaced z values and plot the resulting S-curve.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Create evenly spaced z values across the supplied interval and evaluate the logistic sigmoid formula elementwise.
Plot `z` on the horizontal axis against `sig` on the vertical axis, label the axes `"z"` and `"sigma(z)"`, set the title `"Sigmoid Function"`, and call `plt.show()`.
Look at the sigmoid formula on line 4. `np.exp(-z)` is always positive, so adding it to one gives a denominator greater than one. This maps any real number `z` into the open interval `(0, 1)`.

steps.question: What values does the sigmoid take at `z = 0`, at the supplied large negative z, and at `z = 8` (large positive)?
steps.answer: At `z = 0`, `np.exp(0) = 1`, so the sigmoid is one half. For the large negative z, the exponential is large, so the sigmoid is near zero. At `z = 8`, the exponential is near zero, so the sigmoid is near one.
